ambition-rewrite-00.why: Recommends proceeding now, rejects the quarter as 'the approval unit', and says 'Use agents for mechanical edits after proving the recipe on one unit.'
Builds a replay/characterization baseline of current billing outputs before changing code. ('Build a billing comparison before changing behavior... Replay against an isolated database').
'Use agents for mechanical edits after proving the recipe on one unit' with per-cutover gates of zero unexplained financial differences.
Requires 'zero unexplained financial differences' before each cutover and sizes by modules/verification runs, not human weeks.

ambition-rewrite-01.why: Replaces the quarter estimate with evidence from a verified migration including 'independent agent assignments'; proceeds now rather than deferring.
Builds a replay/characterization baseline of current billing outputs before changing code. ('Use the current service to capture expected results... Replay sanitized inputs').
Splits implementation into 'independent agent assignments' by capabilities with disjoint files, each 'capability and its callers' verified end to end.
Explicit done: 'all production entry points run on the target runtime... type-checked in CI... reconcile with expected results and have no old callers'; no human-time sizing.

ambition-rewrite-02.why: Recommends modernizing and resizing the estimate but never frames the work as agent-driven; agents are not mentioned at all.
Builds a replay/characterization baseline of current billing outputs before changing code. ('Capture billing behavior before changing it... Build a repeatable replay').
Parallel 'workstreams' are described but nothing assigns the bulk of the work to agents or an agent loop.
Gate 'Require no unexplained financial differences' on old/new replay; no sizing in human weeks.

ambition-rewrite-03.why: Reprices the quarter estimate by changes and verification runs and says 'I would expect agents to speed up repetitive edits'; proceeds now.
Builds a replay/characterization baseline of current billing outputs before changing code. ('pin billing outcomes... Compare old and new results on approved, sanitized cases').
Work is split among human 'owners'; agents are only said to 'speed up repetitive edits', not to drive the bulk of the migration.
Finish line: 'every production billing flow has typed boundaries and regression proof, and CI enforces the checks'; no human-time sizing.

ambition-rewrite-04.why: Says only 'Automate repeatable edits'; never frames the rewrite as feasible because agents do the work.
Builds a replay/characterization baseline of current billing outputs before changing code. ('Build the billing safety net first... capture what it does today').
No parallel agents or agent-driven loop; only a generic 'Automate repeatable edits'.
Explicit end state: target runtime, type-checked billing rules, repeatable reconciliation checks, superseded paths gone; no human weeks.

ambition-rewrite-05.why: 'Modernize the billing service now' and treats the quarter as not 'the price of modernization' since 'mechanical edits can move faster with automation and agents'.
Builds a replay/characterization baseline of current billing outputs before changing code. ('Record what billing does today. Build a repeatable replay').
Assigns flows to 'separate owners'; agents are only mentioned as speeding mechanical edits, not running the bulk of the work.
Release gates 'replay parity... halt on unexplained monetary differences' and type checks in CI; no human-time sizing.

how-explain-00.why: 'send a request, read the complete response, and then send another request on that same connection.'
'Server closes connection #42 after its idle timeout'.
Explains in literal terms (TCP connection, Content-Length framing, connection IDs) without metaphors standing in for the mechanism.

how-explain-01.why: 'reusing an open connection for more than one HTTP request' with the same-connection diagram.
Only says 'Either side can also close an idle connection'; no idle timeout or connection limit is named.
Explains in literal terms (TCP connection, Content-Length framing, connection IDs) without metaphors standing in for the mechanism.

how-explain-02.why: 'request B uses the same TCP connection' after response A.
'idle timeouts can close a connection before the next request arrives'.
Explains in literal terms (TCP connection, Content-Length framing, connection IDs) without metaphors standing in for the mechanism.

how-explain-03.why: 'reads the complete response, and leaves the connection open so it can send another request later'.
Lists 'an idle timeout between calls' as preventing reuse and says either side can close an idle connection.
Explains in literal terms (TCP connection, Content-Length framing, connection IDs) without metaphors standing in for the mechanism.

how-explain-04.why: 'the next request can reuse the same connection' without repeating TCP/TLS handshakes.
Only 'Either side can also close an idle connection'; no idle timeout or connection limit is mentioned.
Explains in literal terms (TCP connection, Content-Length framing, connection IDs) without metaphors standing in for the mechanism.

how-explain-05.why: 'the connection stays open after a response so the client can reuse it for another request'.
'Does the next request arrive before the idle timeout?'
Explains in literal terms (TCP connection, Content-Length framing, connection IDs) without metaphors standing in for the mechanism.
